plugins.name: Fleet ACP

description.en: Delegate a task to any Agent Client Protocol v1 coding agent installed on the remote machine.
description.zh: 把任务交给远端机器上已经安装的任意 Agent Client Protocol v1 编码 Agent。

plugins.body:
# Fleet ACP

Fleet ACP is an MIT-licensed bridge between Fleet and Agent Client Protocol v1.
The remote machine owns its ACP-compatible agent, account, model, and API keys.
The plugin only initializes that local process, creates a session, delegates a
prompt, and returns streamed output through the existing Fleet task ticket.
Version 0.1.2 keeps this one-shot task ABI while enforcing hard request,
configuration, ACP frame, update-count, and collected-output limits. It drains
stderr without unbounded retention and propagates shutdown into nested ACP
process groups before forcefully cleaning up the delegated process tree.

Install it by asking an AI connected to Fleet Tool to call `install_plugin` with
`plugin_id` set to `fleet.acp`. The target Agent applies its device permit:
`off` refuses, `ask` prompts locally, and `allow` installs without a second
plugin confirmation. Release and executable SHA-256 checks remain mandatory.

plugins.name: Fleet Transfer

description.en: Send one file directly between two approved Fleet endpoints without relaying file bytes through the Hub.
description.zh: 在两个已确认的 Fleet 端点之间直接传输单个文件，文件字节不经过 Hub 中转。

plugins.body:
# Fleet Transfer

`fleet.transfer` is the official file-system adapter for Fleet's direct-only
file transfer path. Fleet core authenticates the account and endpoints, signs a
short-lived direct-session ticket, and requires one local authorization
decision on each endpoint. A device Agent applies its permit: `off` refuses,
`ask` prompts locally, and `allow` authorizes without another plugin click.
The plugin then reads or writes one regular file through the generic bounded
`fleet.plugin.peer.v1` ABI.

File bytes use a dedicated reliable WebRTC DataChannel. The Worker and Durable
Object carry only authentication, signaling, status, and short-lived tickets.
If a direct connection cannot be established, the transfer fails instead of
falling back to WebSocket, Worker, R2, TURN, or another relay.

Version 0.2.1 keeps manifest, chunk/hash, resume, acknowledgement, and commit
inside the two plugin endpoints' private `fleet.transfer.v2` DATA protocol.
Fleet core preserves opaque DATA frame boundaries and does not understand file
transfer. One file, SHA-256 integrity, verified resume checkpoints, safe
cancellation, no-clobber publication, and idempotent completion retry backed by
a transfer-bound local receipt are supported. Directories, symbolic links,
special files, overwrite, and cross-account transfer remain excluded.
Both endpoints enforce a 10 GiB default local file-size limit. The target also
keeps 1 GiB free by default and rechecks capacity while receiving; operators
may override either byte limit through the plugin process environment.
